measured.Notes: Open decision 1 in MEASUREMENT_PLAN.md. Measured at apex level per ISO, NOT at the largest girth found: on this body the maximum girth sits 20mm above the apex because the ribcage broadens toward the armpits, a 1.1cm difference from wording alone. DIAG_MAX_TORSO_GIRTH reports the other reading for comparison.

Diagnostic only. Shows how far the largest girth drifts from the apex level; a large gap means the bust definition matters for this body.

not_measured.Notes: No HPS landmark can be detected on this mesh. The head is cut off at the neck, so there is no neck-base curve to reference. A 'highest point outboard of the neck' rule was tried and rejected: it returns whatever sits on its own inner cutoff — 35mm gives x=-37.4mm/y=1593.1mm, 45mm gives -45.2/1589.2, 90mm gives -95.9/1534.9 — a 58mm spread in height driven by a parameter with no anatomical basis. That is false precision, so no automatic value is produced.

The breast root is a design decision as much as a geometric fact: where a wire sits at the inner and outer ends is chosen by the TD, not read off the mesh. Only the bottom of the root is derived automatically (the fold section directly below the apex). Place ROOT_INNER and ROOT_OUTER for the side you need and the arc becomes measurable. Inner end to bottom to outer end, along the surface; the sum is the wire length.

Cup volume is measured inside a CLOSED root loop: inner -> bottom -> outer -> top -> inner, each leg a shortest surface path. The loop is a design decision, so three of its four points are placed by hand; the bottom is derived. Place ROOT_INNER, ROOT_OUTER and ROOT_TOP for the side you need. SENSITIVITY, measured: moving ROOT_TOP by ±15mm swings this value from 192.9ml to 271.2ml — about ±18%. The routine itself is accurate to 0.064% against analytic spherical caps, so the number is dominated by WHERE the root loop is placed, not by the maths. Whoever places the loop owns the result; record the loop with the value.
